title: Electric Charges Mindmap
notes: Foundational electrostatics covering nature, quantization, and conservation of electric charge.
Mechanisms of electrification: triboelectric friction, conduction, and electrostatic induction with earthing.
Quantitative electrostatic forces via Coulomb's law, dielectric attenuation, and vector superposition.

subtopics.name: Conservation of Charge
points: Total charge of an isolated system remains strictly constant

subtopics.name: Charging by Friction
points: Triboelectric electron transfer between differing materials
Glass on silk becomes positive; amber/ebonite becomes negative

subtopics.name: Charging by Conduction
points: Charge redistributes until electrostatic potentials equalize

subtopics.name: Charging by Induction
points: Non-contact method utilizing polarization and grounding
Traps charge of opposite polarity on the conductor
Earthing must be disconnected BEFORE removing inducing body

subtopics.name: Scalar & Vector Formulation
points: Vector form: F⃗₁₂ = -F⃗₂₁ (satisfies Newton's third law)

subtopics.name: Medium Effect & Dielectrics
points: Force in dielectric: F_m = F₀ / κ
Dielectric screening explains salt dissolution in water (κ ≈ 80)

subtopics.name: Principle of Superposition
points: Net electrostatic force is vector sum: F⃗_net = ∑ F⃗_i

subtopics.name: Electrostatic Equilibrium
points: Earnshaw's Theorem: Stable equilibrium impossible with static charges alone
